proposals.mechanism_name: Cross-asset cointegration relative value with a long spot and short USD-M perpetual pair
proposals.economic_premise: Some cryptocurrency prices may share a time-varying long-run relation. A temporary spread displacement can therefore contain a convergence component distinct from outright market direction. Aurex would express only the orientation that buys the relatively underpriced asset in cash spot and shorts the relatively overpriced asset through its USD-M perpetual, avoiding spot borrowing while retaining cross-asset model, basis, funding, and collateral risk.
proposals.ex_ante_payoff_direction: The paired position can profit only when the frozen spread converges enough to exceed both-leg fees, spread, adverse execution, funding, hedge-ratio error, collateral drag, and model-break risk. Cointegration does not guarantee convergence during the holding window.
proposals.execution_path: At a later frozen signal time, buy the underpriced asset in cash-funded spot and short the overvalued asset's USD-M perpetual using a separately audited cross-asset hedge ratio. Require paired fills, rollback on a failed leg, isolated collateral, funding settlement, mark-based risk, capacity limits, kill switches, and deterministic close reconciliation.
proposals.pre_return_falsification_condition: Reject before primary selection if fewer than twenty symbols satisfy the frozen synchronized timestamp coverage contract, if historical funding and execution dependencies cannot be reconstructed, or if Aurex cannot prove a deterministic long-spot short-cross-asset-perpetual lifecycle with one predeclared pair-selection and parameter policy.
independence_from_blocked_lineages: Funding is modeled only as a cost or receipt on the short leg and is not the signal or the proposed source of edge.
The premise is spread stationarity and cross-asset convergence, not trend, breakout, path quality, broad beta timing, or funding carry.

coverage_contract.timestamp_join_policy: Exact UTC symbol and one-minute open-time inner join for every required price family; funding joins only at settled event times.
coverage_contract.missing_row_policy: Never fill a missing row. A missing synchronized decision minute is untradable and skipped; a gap exceeding the frozen maximum resets formation state and disqualifies the affected calendar month.

primary_sources.title: Copula-based trading of cointegrated cryptocurrency pairs
supported_claims: Cointegration and copula methods can define relative-value relationships among cryptocurrency prices.
Pair formation, ranking, triggers, and transaction costs are material parts of an implementable pairs study.

primary_sources.title: Common dynamic factors for cryptocurrencies and multiple pair-trading statistical arbitrages
supported_claims: Cryptocurrency prices can exhibit common dynamic factors and cointegration relationships.
Relative-value construction remains model-dependent and requires explicit multivariate estimation.

primary_sources.title: On cointegration and cryptocurrency dynamics
supported_claims: A dynamic relation cannot be treated as guaranteed terminal convergence.
Cointegration exposure in cryptocurrency systems can vary through time rather than remain fixed.

proposals.mechanism_name: Clock-phase intraday predictability around recurring algorithmic activity windows
proposals.economic_premise: Continuous cryptocurrency venues can still exhibit recurring bursts in algorithmic activity, volume, volatility, and serial dependence near fixed clock boundaries. A strictly preregistered UTC clock-phase rule could test whether this scheduled activity supplies directional information after costs, but the documented sign changes across regimes and may overlap momentum or reversal rather than represent a durable edge.
proposals.ex_ante_payoff_direction: A later rule could earn only if the return direction associated with a predeclared clock phase persists out of sample and exceeds taker costs, spread, adverse execution, funding, and directional drawdown. Recurring activity or volatility alone does not imply positive return expectancy.
proposals.execution_path: A later separately frozen engine would take a bounded long or short USD-M perpetual position only at a predeclared UTC phase, use taker fills with adverse costs, settle funding when crossed, apply isolated margin and hard loss limits, and close at an exact time rather than an outcome-conditioned technical exit.
proposals.pre_return_falsification_condition: Reject before primary selection if complete aggregate-trade history cannot distinguish clock-phase activity and signed order flow, if fewer than ten contracts satisfy the frozen coverage floor, if standalone directional futures risk is not deterministically modeled, or if the premise cannot be separated from a retired momentum or reversal rule.
independence_from_blocked_lineages: Any sign or horizon must come from theory before Aurex outcomes and cannot be selected among momentum and reversal variants.
The proposed cause is scheduled algorithmic clock activity rather than price trend, breakout, broad beta, or funding carry.

coverage_contract.timestamp_join_policy: Exact UTC trade timestamp aggregation into one-minute and fixed quarter-hour clock phases joined to closed perpetual minutes.
coverage_contract.missing_row_policy: Never fill missing trades or candles. Exclude the affected clock event and reject a symbol-month when a gap exceeds fifteen minutes.

primary_sources.title: The Quarter-Hour Effect: Periodic Algorithmic Trading and Return Predictability in Cryptocurrency Futures
supported_claims: Crypto futures activity can cluster at fixed one-, five-, and fifteen-minute clock boundaries.
Order imbalance, not the clock label alone, is part of the reported return-prediction mechanism.

primary_sources.title: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both
supported_claims: Intraday cryptocurrency predictability has included both momentum and reversal.
Jumps, liquidity, macro announcements, and regimes can change the observed pattern.

primary_sources.title: Revisiting seasonality in cryptocurrencies
supported_claims: A clock-based proposal requires strong falsification and cannot assume stable return direction.
Cryptocurrency calendar and seasonal effects have not been uniformly robust across specifications.

proposals.mechanism_name: Passive limit-order liquidity provision with queue and toxicity control
proposals.economic_premise: A passive market maker can earn the bid-ask spread for supplying liquidity, but the compensation exists only against uncertain fills, queue priority, adverse selection, inventory, cancellation latency, and fees. Candle-based apparent spread capture is not executable evidence; the mechanism requires event-level order-book and own-order state.
proposals.ex_ante_payoff_direction: Expected spread and maker rebates must exceed adverse post-fill price movement, missed fills, inventory liquidation, queue decay, latency, cancellation failures, and exchange fees. High fill probability can coincide with more toxic fills rather than higher profit.
proposals.execution_path: Continuously quote bounded bid and ask orders only after reconstructing price-time priority, own queue position, acknowledgements, partial fills, cancellations, rejects, latency, inventory, toxicity, fees, and emergency flattening. Every simulated fill must be justified by event sequence rather than candle high-low contact.
proposals.pre_return_falsification_condition: Reject before primary selection unless immutable historical L2 updates, trades, sequence continuity, queue reconstruction, dated maker fees, and own-order-equivalent fill semantics are available at sufficient resolution. One-minute OHLCV or top-of-book snapshots cannot substitute.
independence_from_blocked_lineages: The edge can be evaluated only from queue-aware passive fills and cannot inherit any candle-based Aurex outcome.
The premise is compensation for executable liquidity supply, not directional trend, breakout, reversal timing, beta, or funding carry.

coverage_contract.timestamp_join_policy: Strict exchange sequence and subsecond event-time replay joining book updates, trades, and own-order-equivalent lifecycle events.
coverage_contract.missing_row_policy: Never infer a book update, queue position, fill, or cancellation. Any sequence gap stops the affected session and source feasibility.

primary_sources.title: The Market Maker's Dilemma: Navigating the Fill Probability vs. Post-Fill Returns Trade-Off
supported_claims: A live Binance Bitcoin perpetual experiment finds a trade-off between passive fill likelihood and post-fill returns.
Queue sizes, queue position, and immediate price dynamics are required to evaluate maker fills.

primary_sources.title: Do Order-Book States Predict Passive-Buy Toxicity? Evidence from BTC Perpetual Futures
supported_claims: L2 snapshots and aggregate trades are necessary inputs to the reported empirical design.
Passive-fill toxicity depends on local order flow, displayed support, and liquidity fragility.

primary_sources.title: Adverse Selection in Cryptocurrency Markets
supported_claims: Cryptocurrency limit-order markets exhibit economically meaningful adverse-selection costs.
Order and trade data are needed to estimate effective spread and information asymmetry.

limitations: Candidate, validation, holdout, forward, Pine, paper, sandbox, live, and capital permissions remain false.
Clock-phase evidence is mixed and requires aggregate trades plus a separate directional futures foundation.
Cointegration remains model-dependent and requires a separate cross-asset paired execution foundation plus multiplicity controls.
Coverage thresholds were frozen before a proposal-specific coverage result and cannot be relaxed after observing feasibility.
No price value, parameter, signal, trade, P/L, or return was inspected or calculated.
Passive liquidity provision remains blocked unless historical L2, queue, fill, latency, and dated maker-fee evidence is qualified.
Registration freezes theory and source requirements only and makes no claim that any proposal is profitable or selectable.
